title: A relativistic von Kármán relation for assessing applicability of hydrodynamics
summary: Relativistic viscous hydrodynamics is a widely used theoretical framework for simulating quark-gluon plasma (QGP) dynamics in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. One open question is how to quantitatively assess the validity of a hydrodynamic description of such a system. In this work, we extract the poles of linear response functions from numerical simulations of hydrodynamics and Boltzmann transport. By comparing these responses as a function of the rescaled wavenumber $\bar{k}$, we identify the wavenumber range over which hydrodynamics captures the underlying microscopic dynamics. We show that the averaged Knudsen number, $\langle\mathrm{Kn}^{*}\rangle$, which we define using the von Kármán relation, serves as a measure of $\bar{k}$. We find that $\langle\mathrm{Kn}^{*}\rangle_{\rm max}\sim 1$ marks the approximate upper limit of agreement between the linear responses of second-order viscous hydrodynamics and Boltzmann transport.

title: Nuclear Shell Model on the Light Front
summary: Light-front descriptions of nuclear structure provide a relativistic framework that can potentially deepen our understanding of nuclear structure by revealing effects that are absent from traditional non-relativistic treatments. To utilize this framework, we start from the light-front harmonic oscillator to analytically calculate the shell structure and electromagnetic form factors. The relativistic shell model shows that the light-front result recovers the nonrelativistic oscillator limit while introducing shell splitting that depends on the longitudinal excitation quantum number. We derive the resulting effects on the shell model and use the Hellmann-Feynman theorem to identify the longitudinal confinement interaction as the origin of this splitting. We illustrate these results through applications to $^{48}\mathrm{Ca}$ and $^{208}\mathrm{Pb}$. In addition, we demonstrate a substantial difference between form factors calculated using non-relativistic and light-front treatments, a difference that further underscores the importance of including relativistic effects in the description of nuclear structure. Our findings demonstrate a tractable approach to relativistic nuclear calculations and show how extending nuclear models beyond the non-relativistic approximation can yield meaningful physical insight.

title: u4lib: An AI-Ready Computational Framework for U(4) Symmetry Algebra, Wigner Coupling, and Racah Recoupling Coefficients
comment: 16 pages, 1 figure, 3 tables. Source code available at https://github.com/Deep-SANE/u4lib. Companion to the u3lib manual, arXiv:2611.26558
summary: Wigner's supermultiplet symmetry treats nucleon spin and isospin within a common U(4)/SU(4) description. The C++ library u4lib supplies the coupling coefficients and algebraic operations needed for calculations in this scheme. Users can construct irreducible representations (irreps), obtain dimensions and Casimir invariants, conjugate states, enumerate the canonical Gelfand-Tsetlin and physical $\mathrm{SU_S(2)}\otimes\mathrm{SU_T(2)}$ bases with inner multiplicities, and decompose tensor products. Matrix-element routines cover the canonical U(4) generators and the physical spin $\mathbf{S}$, isospin $\mathbf{T}$, and Gamow-Teller-type tensor $\mathbf{U}$. Wigner coupling and Racah recoupling coefficients are evaluated by the 2024 procedure of Dang et al. The implementation builds on u3lib, with a header-only C++ interface and corresponding Python bindings. A catalog of agent skills assists an AI agent in preparing, executing, and checking calculations through natural-language requests.

title: Thermal photon production in massless boost-invariant gases: hydrodynamization without thermalization
summary: We study hydrodynamization and thermalization in ultrarelativistic heavy-ion collisions using relativistic kinetic theory. Modelling the quark-gluon plasma as a classical gas of massless particles undergoing a boost-invariant longitudinal expansion, we solve the Boltzmann equation in the relaxation-time approximation via a semi-analytical method based on the method of moments. We show that the energy-momentum tensor is well described by relativistic fluid dynamics even when the system is far from local equilibrium. The single-particle distribution function, on the other hand, is not well approximated by a hydrodynamic truncation, suggesting that the onset of hydrodynamic behaviour does not require thermalization. We then quantify how the departure from equilibrium affects the emission rate of thermal photons in the forward scattering approximation, and show that non-equilibrium corrections beyond the hydrodynamic limit can have a significant impact on this observable.

title: Study of two-photon femtoscopic correlations in Ag+Ag collisions at $\mathbf{\sqrt{s_{NN}}}$ = 2.55 GeV with HADES
summary: Two-photon correlations can provide unique femtoscopic information, complementing those obtained with charged particles. They also allow to estimate the direct photon yield in the low $p_{T}$ region. We present experimental results on $γ-γ$ correlations in Ag+Ag collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}$ = 2.55 GeV, collected by the HADES experiment. Photons were measured using an electromagnetic calorimeter (ECAL) and two-photon correlations were determined as one-dimen-sional functions $CF(q_{inv})$. We discuss the observed structures, along with their plausible origin. Finally, we estimate an upper limit for the correlation strength of direct photons for two confidence levels, resulting in values of the order $10^{-4}-10^{-3}$ .

title: Nuclear Urca cooling in magnetar crust and anomalous heating
summary: We present a new result that the nuclear Urca process in magnetars, associated with ultrastrong magnetic field, dramatically alters the neutrino cooling efficiency to support higher surface temper ature, which is not common in ordinary neutron stars. A new formalism for neutrino luminosity accommodating finite temperature on top of magnetic field is extended with the use of realistic nuclear structure inputs for the Urca pair 29Na-29Mg. We find that the neutrino luminosity of Urca pair shows a spiral variation as a function of magnetic field and crust density, while the Urca pair persists, in contrast to previous studies. Applying geometrically correct volumetric energy loss rate to Urca shell at fixed density with varying magnetic field strength, our results show that thermally populated excited states at finite temperature enhance neutrino luminosity, whereas conditions con strained Urca-pair formation driven by ultrastrong magnetic field reduce cooling efficiency, which can explain high temperature of magnetar surface as a new possibility.

title: Soft--hard Bayesian inference in heavy-ion collisions
comment: 6 pages, 3 figures. Contribution to the proceedings of Hard Probes 2026 (Nashville, Tennessee, 21-26 June 2026)
summary: Bayesian analyses of jet quenching commonly constrain jet--medium interaction parameters using a fixed quark-gluon plasma (QGP) background obtained from a soft-sector calibration. This approach neglects uncertainty in the medium and prevents hard observables from providing additional constraints on its properties. We investigate these effects in Pb--Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=2.76$ TeV using sequential Bayesian inference in a reduced three-parameter space. We vary the initial normalization and nucleon width of the medium together with the jet--medium coupling, combining JETSCAPE medium evolution with MATTER+LBT calculations of high-$p_T$ hadron and inclusive-jet suppression. We first constrain all three parameters using the hard observables alone, then incorporate a projected soft-sector posterior through sequential inference. We find that the hard observables are sensitive to the medium properties and reveal substantial correlations with the jet--medium coupling, reflecting their compensating effects on jet quenching. Propagating the soft-sector information shifts the preferred coupling relative to a fixed-medium extraction, with the update driven primarily by hadron-suppression measurements. Despite substantial differences in the medium parameters and coupling favored by hard-observable-only and sequential inference, their suppression predictions remain similar over much of the measured range. These findings highlight the difficulty of distinguishing changes in the QGP medium from changes in microscopic jet--medium interaction strength using inclusive suppression measurements alone.

title: Nuclear Precision and Multimessenger Constraints on Neutron-Star Structure
summary: Neutron-star cores retain structural freedom beyond the constraints supplied by nuclear measurements. We quantify this freedom through an observable-dependent variance ceiling and identify radius--Love compensation as a mechanism suppressing nuclear constraints on tides. Across four data-conditioned equation-of-state families, a pulsar radius measured to 0.3 km paired with a binary tide measured to 10\% removes 44--68\% of the current logarithmic Love-number variance. The framework connects laboratory precision and complementary stellar measurements to core structure.
